dataset_id.description:
A unique ID for this dataset, without the project name. The ID
must contain only letters (a-z, A-Z), numbers (0-9), or
underscores (_). The maximum length is 1,024 characters.
dataset_id.rationale: dataset_id defines the dataset to which IAM policies are applied

default_collation.description:
Defines the default collation specification of future tables created
in the dataset. If a table is created in this dataset without table-level
default collation, then the table inherits the dataset default collation,
which is applied to the string fields that do not have explicit collation
specified. A change to this field affects only tables created afterwards,
and does not alter the existing tables.

The following values are supported:
- 'und:ci': undetermined locale, case insensitive.
- '': empty string. Default to case-sensitive behavior.
default_collation.rationale: Controls string comparison and sorting behaviour for future tables. It does not directly change access control, encryption, data exposure, retention, or resource availability.

default_partition_expiration_ms.description:
The default partition expiration for all partitioned tables in
the dataset, in milliseconds.
Once this property is set, all newly-created partitioned tables in
the dataset will have an 'expirationMs' property in the 'timePartitioning'
settings set to this value, and changing the value will only
affect new tables, not existing ones. The storage in a partition will
have an expiration time of its partition time plus this value.
Setting this property overrides the use of 'defaultTableExpirationMs'
for partitioned tables: only one of 'defaultTableExpirationMs' and
'defaultPartitionExpirationMs' will be used for any new partitioned
table. If you provide an explicit 'timePartitioning.expirationMs' when
creating or updating a partitioned table, that value takes precedence
over the default partition expiration time indicated by this property.
default_partition_expiration_ms.rationale: Partition expiration length is an operational data-management and retention choice left to individual teams. It is not a security control that PDE should enforce centrally.

default_table_expiration_ms.description:
The default lifetime of all tables in the dataset, in milliseconds.
The minimum value is 3600000 milliseconds (one hour).
Once this property is set, all newly-created tables in the dataset
will have an 'expirationTime' property set to the creation time plus
the value in this property, and changing the value will only affect
new tables, not existing ones. When the 'expirationTime' for a given
table is reached, that table will be deleted automatically.
If a table's 'expirationTime' is modified or removed before the
table expires, or if you provide an explicit 'expirationTime' when
creating a table, that value takes precedence over the default
expiration time indicated by this property.
default_table_expiration_ms.rationale: The default table lifespan is a team data-management and retention choice. It is separate from destructive resource-protection controls and should not be enforced as a security policy.

delete_contents_on_destroy.description:
If set to 'true', delete all the tables in the
dataset when destroying the resource; otherwise,
destroying the resource will fail if tables are present.
delete_contents_on_destroy.rationale: When true, Terraform can delete the dataset together with all contained tables. A policy should normally require false unless destructive deletion has been explicitly approved.

deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether Terraform can delete, abandon, or protect the dataset. Requiring PREVENT for protected environments reduces accidental deletion and loss of Terraform management.

description.description: A user-friendly description of the dataset
description.rationale: Human-readable metadata only. It does not alter permissions, encryption, network exposure, retention, or other security controls.

friendly_name.description: A descriptive name for the dataset
friendly_name.rationale: Display metadata only. It does not affect access control, encryption, data exposure, retention, or resource behaviour.

is_case_insensitive.description:
TRUE if the dataset and its table names are case-insensitive, otherwise FALSE.
By default, this is FALSE, which means the dataset and its table names are
case-sensitive. This field does not affect routine references.
is_case_insensitive.rationale: Controls name matching for datasets and tables. It does not directly grant access or change a security, compliance, encryption, or retention control.

labels.description:
The labels associated with this dataset. You can use these to
organize and group your datasets.


**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Labels are organisational metadata and this field is non-authoritative. They do not directly enforce access control or another security boundary; organisation-specific labelling requirements are better handled by governance rules.

location.description:
The geographic location where the dataset should reside.
See [official docs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/dataset-locations).
There are two types of locations, regional or multi-regional. A regional
location is a specific geographic place, such as Tokyo, and a multi-regional
location is a large geographic area, such as the United States, that
contains at least two geographic places.
The default value is multi-regional location 'US'.
Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
location.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

max_time_travel_hours.description: Defines the time travel window in hours. The value can be from 48 to 168 hours (2 to 7 days).
max_time_travel_hours.rationale: The time-travel window is a backup-retention and data-recovery choice made by the team. It is an operational setting rather than a centrally enforceable security control.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the project that owns the dataset but is not inherently insecure by itself. The approved project list is organisation-specific, and the field does not directly grant dataset access.

resource_tags.description:
The tags attached to this table. Tag keys are globally unique. Tag key is expected to be
in the namespaced format, for example "123456789012/environment" where 123456789012 is the
ID of the parent organization or project resource for this tag key. Tag value is expected
to be the short name, for example "Production". See [Tag definitions](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/tags-access-control#definitions)
for more details.
resource_tags.rationale: Resource tags are organisation-specific metadata and reference values. PDE cannot centrally determine the required tag keys or values, so this field should not be a generic policy target.

storage_billing_model.description:
Specifies the storage billing model for the dataset.
Set this flag value to LOGICAL to use logical bytes for storage billing,
or to PHYSICAL to use physical bytes instead.

LOGICAL is the default if this flag isn't specified.
storage_billing_model.rationale: Controls whether storage is billed using logical or physical bytes. It affects cost calculation rather than confidentiality, integrity, access control, encryption, or availability.

access.description: An array of objects that define dataset access for one or more entities.

access.domain.description:
A domain to grant access to. Any users signed in with the
domain specified will be granted the specified access
access.domain.rationale: Grants dataset access to every signed-in user in a domain, which is broader than a named principal. A policy should restrict domains to an approved allowlist.

access.group_by_email.description: An email address of a Google Group to grant access to.
access.group_by_email.rationale: Identifies a specific Google Group. Whether that group is authorised is organisation-specific and cannot be determined generically from the email value alone.

access.iam_member.description:
Some other type of member that appears in the IAM Policy but isn't a user,
group, domain, or special group. For example: 'allUsers'
access.iam_member.rationale: Can contain broad or public principals such as allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers. A policy should reject public principals and other prohibited member patterns.

access.role.description:
Describes the rights granted to the user specified by the other
member of the access object. Basic, predefined, and custom roles
are supported. Predefined roles that have equivalent basic roles
are swapped by the API to their basic counterparts. See
[official docs](https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/access-control).
access.role.rationale: Role selection is the responsibility of the team configuring access. Platform policy should police unsafe principals where applicable, but should not centrally restrict which roles teams may grant.

access.special_group.description:
A special group to grant access to. Possible values include:
* 'projectOwners': Owners of the enclosing project.
* 'projectReaders': Readers of the enclosing project.
* 'projectWriters': Writers of the enclosing project.
* 'allAuthenticatedUsers': All authenticated BigQuery users.
access.special_group.rationale: Can grant access to broad groups such as allAuthenticatedUsers or project-wide owner, writer, and reader groups. A policy should deny prohibited broad groups or restrict them to an approved set.

access.user_by_email.description:
An email address of a user to grant access to. For example:
fred@example.com
access.user_by_email.rationale: Grants dataset access to a specific user by email. It is a specific (non-public) principal; we cannot constrain which user generically without hardcoding an email, and a single user grant is not a public/wildcard exposure, so there is nothing useful to enforce.

access.condition.description:
Condition for the binding. If CEL expression in this field is true, this
access binding will be considered.

access.condition.description.description:
Description of the expression. This is a longer text which describes the expression,
e.g. when hovered over it in a UI.
access.condition.description.rationale: Descriptive metadata for the access condition. It does not change whether the condition evaluates to true or what permissions are granted.

access.condition.expression.description: Textual representation of an expression in Common Expression Language syntax.
access.condition.expression.rationale: Controls when the access binding applies. An empty, unconditional, or overly broad expression can make restricted access effectively unconditional, so a policy should reject clearly unsafe expressions and require an approved condition pattern.

access.condition.location.description:
String indicating the location of the expression for error reporting, e.g. a file
name and a position in the file.
access.condition.location.rationale: Used only to identify the source location of the expression for error reporting. It does not affect authorisation decisions.

access.condition.title.description:
Title for the expression, i.e. a short string describing its purpose.
This can be used e.g. in UIs which allow to enter the expression.
access.condition.title.rationale: Human-readable metadata for the condition. It does not affect condition evaluation or granted permissions.

access.dataset.description: Grants all resources of particular types in a particular dataset read access to the current dataset.

access.dataset.target_types.description:
Which resources in the dataset this entry applies to. Currently, only views are supported,
but additional target types may be added in the future. Possible values: VIEWS
access.dataset.target_types.rationale: Specifies the supported authorised-dataset resource type and currently only accepts VIEWS. The provider already constrains the value, so no separate security policy is useful.

access.dataset.dataset.description: The dataset this entry applies to

access.dataset.dataset.dataset_id.description: The ID of the dataset containing this table.
access.dataset.dataset.dataset_id.rationale: Identifies the authorised dataset. Whether a particular dataset is trusted is organisation-specific and cannot be determined generically from the identifier alone.

access.dataset.dataset.project_id.description: The ID of the project containing this table.
access.dataset.dataset.project_id.rationale: Identifies the project containing the authorised dataset. Whether the project is trusted requires an organisation-specific allowlist; the identifier is not inherently insecure by itself.

access.routine.description:
A routine from a different dataset to grant access to. Queries
executed against that routine will have read access to tables in
this dataset. The role field is not required when this field is
set. If that routine is updated by any user, access to the routine
needs to be granted again via an update operation.

access.routine.dataset_id.description: The ID of the dataset containing this table.
access.routine.dataset_id.rationale: Identifies the dataset containing an authorised routine. Whether that dataset is trusted is organisation-specific and cannot be determined generically from the identifier alone.

access.routine.project_id.description: The ID of the project containing this table.
access.routine.project_id.rationale: Identifies the project containing an authorised routine. Whether the project is approved requires organisation-specific context rather than a universal security rule.

access.routine.routine_id.description:
The ID of the routine. The ID must contain only letters (a-z,
A-Z), numbers (0-9), or underscores (_). The maximum length
is 256 characters.
access.routine.routine_id.rationale: Identifies a specific authorised routine. The identifier itself does not describe the routine's behaviour or prove whether it is trusted.

access.view.description:
A view from a different dataset to grant access to. Queries
executed against that view will have read access to tables in
this dataset. The role field is not required when this field is
set. If that view is updated by any user, access to the view
needs to be granted again via an update operation.

access.view.dataset_id.description: The ID of the dataset containing this table.
access.view.dataset_id.rationale: Identifies the dataset containing an authorised view. Whether the dataset is trusted is organisation-specific and cannot be inferred from the identifier alone.

access.view.project_id.description: The ID of the project containing this table.
access.view.project_id.rationale: Identifies the project containing an authorised view. Whether the project is approved requires organisation-specific context rather than a universal security rule.

access.view.table_id.description:
The ID of the table. The ID must contain only letters (a-z,
A-Z), numbers (0-9), or underscores (_). The maximum length
is 1,024 characters.
access.view.table_id.rationale: Identifies the authorised view. The identifier itself does not reveal whether the view exposes sensitive data or is approved.

default_encryption_configuration.description:
The default encryption key for all tables in the dataset. Once this property is set,
all newly-created partitioned tables in the dataset will have encryption key set to
this value, unless table creation request (or query) overrides the key.

default_encryption_configuration.kms_key.description:
Describes the Cloud KMS encryption key that will be used to protect destination
BigQuery table. The BigQuery Service Account associated with your project requires
access to this encryption key.
default_encryption_configuration.kms_key.rationale: KMS key is used for encryption of data at rest

external_catalog_dataset_options.description:
Options defining open source compatible datasets living in the BigQuery catalog. Contains
metadata of open source database, schema or namespace represented by the current dataset.

external_catalog_dataset_options.default.description:
The storage location URI for all tables in the dataset. Equivalent to hive metastore's
database locationUri. Maximum length of 1024 characters.
external_catalog_dataset_options.default.rationale: This field is a reference to an external storage URI or endpoint. References to external resources and paths are not generic PDE policy targets because approved locations are organisation-specific.

external_catalog_dataset_options.paramet.description:
A map of key value pairs defining the parameters and properties of the open source schema.
Maximum size of 2Mib.
external_catalog_dataset_options.paramet.rationale: Contains implementation-specific catalog metadata. The keys and meanings vary by external catalog, so there is no reliable generic security rule for the map as a whole.

external_dataset_reference.description: Information about the external metadata storage where the dataset is defined.

external_dataset_reference.connection.description:
The connection id that is used to access the externalSource.
Format: projects/{projectId}/locations/{locationId}/connections/{connectionId}
external_dataset_reference.connection.rationale: This argument identifies another resource, a BigQuery connection. PDE guidance treats references to other resources as non-policy targets and does not pin specific resource identifiers.

external_dataset_reference.external_sour.description: External source that backs this dataset.
external_dataset_reference.external_sour.rationale: This field identifies an external data source or naming pointer. PDE does not constrain external resource references or organisation-specific source identifiers through a generic policy.
